maraviroc (a CCR5 receptor antagonist used to treat HIV) exhibits significant drug interactions with other drugs that are inhibitors of CYP3a and P-glycoproteins, and also with drugs that induce CYP3a.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MVC is an OATP1b1 substrate, a P-gp substrate, and a CYP3A4 substrate, and TVR is an OAT1b1 inhibitor, a CYP3a4 inhibitor, and a P-gp inhibitor.
MVC disposition involves intestinal and hepatic interplay of P-gp and OATP, and CYP3A is a significant determinant of MVC disposition.
MVC is a substrate for OATP1A2, OATP1C1, OATP2A1, and OATPB1, and is an inhibitor of P-gp, OATPB1 and OAT1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PBPK model developed in this study provides a mechanistic basis for the prediction and understanding of complex MVC DDIs.
the present study demonstrates that the in vitro mechanistic information on the contribution of CYP3As and transporters (P-gp, OATP1Bs) is critical in predicting the DDI magnitude for MVC.
the PBPK model can be used to predict the DDIs for MVC with multiple drugs and that OATP-mediated hepatic uptake plays a significant role in determining the overall disposition of MVC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contribution of OATP to the overall clearance of MVC is significant, which is not reflected in in vitro intrinsic clearance values.
the contribution of OATP-mediated uptake to hepatic clearance should be considered when evaluating the DDIs of substrates with high OATP1-mediated uptake.
a mechanistic PBPK model that accounts for multiple transporters and metabolizing enzymes can accurately predict the magnitude of MVC DDIs with a wide range of perpetrator drugs.
